items.title: Edmonton fails to meet climate targets 2 years after launching carbon budget (CBC News, Natasha Riebe)

citations.finding: The prior-year miss was also on the record: 2023 community emissions were an estimated 16.2 million tonnes CO2e against a 13.4 million tonne aim, per the Fall 2024 carbon budget update as reported by CBC, which quoted the report: 'If Edmonton's current emission trajectory continues, Edmonton's GHG reduction targets will not be achieved.'
citations.establishes: That the off-track finding is a multi-year pattern (2023 and 2024 both missed), not a one-year anomaly, and was publicly reported from the City's own Fall 2024 update (FCS02532).

citations.finding: The City has implemented measures and policies to curb emissions, including new zoning bylaws, building energy retrofits, and solar panel installations.
citations.establishes: The City is actively taking policy steps, which may be conflated with actually meeting numerical targets.
citations.quote: For example, policies promote more energy-saving buildings, installing solar panels and transitioning from diesel to hydrogen or electric buses, he said.

items.title: Fall 2025 Carbon Budget Update, 2023-2026 Carbon Budget (FCS03160), pp. 2, 4
items.publisher: City of Edmonton, Financial and Corporate Services

citations.finding: Per-capita community emissions have fallen substantially: 12.8 tonnes CO2e per person in 2024, a 46% decrease from the 2005 baseline, and absolute community emissions are 9% below 2005. Per-capita energy use is 27% below the 2005 baseline.
citations.establishes: Some measured progress relative to 2005, mainly per capita. It does not establish being on track: the absolute reduction (9%) is far short of the 35%-by-2025 target trajectory.

citations.finding: The City has funded and launched emissions-reduction initiatives: the 2023-2026 budgets included projects estimated to cut community GHG emissions by about 180,000 tonnes CO2e over four years, plus programs such as the Clean Energy Improvement Program and a new zoning bylaw.
citations.establishes: That the City is taking some funded climate action. The scale (180,000 t over four years) is roughly 1% of one year of community emissions (15.2 Mt), so it does not establish being on track.

citations.finding: The City's own Fall 2025 Carbon Budget Update reports 2024 community emissions of 15.2 million tCO2e (a 3% increase from 2023) against a 2024 target-trajectory value of 12.2 million tCO2e or less. The 2024 target was not met. Meeting the 2025 target would require cutting to 10.8 million tCO2e, a 29% reduction in a single year.
citations.establishes: The latest published inventory (2024) is roughly 25% above the City's own required trajectory for that year, and the 2025 milestone is out of reach on the City's own assessment. This is the City contradicting its own goal.
citations.quote: The trend for this year indicates this target will not be met and there are no current initiatives or actions that will allow the necessary reductions to meet the target.

citations.finding: The community carbon budget of 176 million tonnes CO2e (the total allowed 2022-2050 to reach neutrality by 2050) is forecast to be fully depleted by 2036, one year earlier than the original 2023-2026 Carbon Budget forecast of 2037. The report concludes further action is needed to achieve community and corporate targets.
citations.establishes: On the City's own forecast, the entire 2050 emissions allowance will be spent by 2036, and the trajectory is worsening slightly, not improving, relative to the original plan.
citations.quote: The Carbon Budget continues to deplete at a rate consistent with prior projections, which is expected to hinder the City's ability to achieve established reduction targets.

citations.finding: A previously claimed win was retracted: the Fall 2024 update said per-capita energy use had fallen 40%, surpassing the 2030 energy-efficiency target, but after the 2005 baseline was recalculated with revised natural gas data, the 2024 inventory shows that target has NOT been reached (current reduction: 27%).
citations.establishes: The one Energy Transition Strategy sub-target the City had reported as achieved was withdrawn after a data revision, removing the strongest candidate for a 'meeting its goals' example.

citations.finding: Corporate (City-operations) emissions, tracked separately, are also over budget: quantified 2023-2026 corporate emissions of 884,000 tonnes CO2e exceed the roughly 816,000-tonne corporate budget, a 68,000-tonne carbon deficit, with the corporate carbon budget forecast depleted in 2032 versus the 2040 neutrality target. Corporate emissions are about 2% of community emissions.
citations.establishes: Context only (a different measure from the community target): the City is off track on its own operations too, so the miss is not confined to emissions outside municipal control.

citations.finding: The 2023-2026 approved budgets funded projects estimated to reduce community emissions by 180,000 tCO2e over four years, and the City reported several energy-transition initiatives underway.
citations.establishes: The City funded and implemented measures intended to reduce emissions. The quantified reduction is a forecast, not an observed outcome, and the same report says it is insufficient to put Edmonton on track.

citations.finding: The City's public climate strategies page states the targets (35% by 2025, 50% by 2030, net zero per person by 2050) and describes the city as 'just starting to accelerate our journey,' without claiming targets are being met.
citations.establishes: Even the City's public-facing communications do not assert the community targets are on track.

citations.finding: The latest inventory reported 2024 community emissions of 15.2 million tCO2e against a required 2024 trajectory value of no more than 12.2 million tCO2e. The City expressly assessed Edmonton as off track for every adopted emissions milestone.
citations.establishes: The latest reported community inventory exceeded the City's trajectory by 3.0 million tCO2e, and the City's own assessment says Edmonton is not on track.
citations.quote: GHG emissions are not decreasing over time and are not on track to meet the 2025, 2030 and 2050 emissions targets.

citations.finding: The City forecasts that the remaining community carbon budget will be depleted in 2036, well before the 2050 target year.
citations.establishes: The City's forecast is inconsistent with remaining within the adopted cumulative community carbon budget through 2050.

items.title: City of Edmonton Financial Annual Report 2025
items.source_date: 2026, covering the 2025 reporting year and 2024 GHG inventory

citations.finding: The 2024 community inventory reported total emissions nine per cent below the recalculated 2005 baseline and per-capita emissions 46 per cent below the baseline.
citations.establishes: Edmonton has reduced total and per-capita community emissions relative to 2005. It does not establish that reductions are occurring at the rate required by the adopted trajectory.

citations.finding: The City's 2026 climate-plan review says the existing targets remain aligned with best practice and will not be revised, while its FAQ acknowledges that Edmonton is unlikely to meet the 2025 target.
citations.establishes: The City had not replaced the adopted targets as of September 2026 and continued to acknowledge the missed or likely missed 2025 milestone.
citations.quote: Will you update the City's climate targets given the City is unlikely to meet its 2025 GHG emissions reduction target?

items.title: Climate Action Plan Update (2027-2030), Engaged Edmonton

citations.finding: The City maintains active climate strategies (Community Energy Transition Strategy; Climate Resilient Edmonton) and is preparing a Climate Action Plan Update with priority actions for 2027-2030, with public engagement December 5, 2025 to January 30, 2026 and a final plan to Council in mid-2026.
citations.establishes: Intent to continue and update climate planning. Establishes nothing about whether targets are being met.

items.title: 2023-2026 Carbon Budget (FCS01478), pp. 2, 4
items.publisher: City of Edmonton, Financial and Corporate Services

citations.finding: The adopted targets themselves: 'the City of Edmonton's community emission reduction targets are 35 per cent by 2025, 50 per cent by 2030 (both from 2005 baseline levels) and becoming an emissions neutral community by 2050,' with a 176 Mt CO2e community carbon budget for 2022-2050. The same report already warned in 2022 that 'current investments are not enough to achieve reduction targets.'
citations.establishes: The benchmark the claim is measured against (what the targets are), and that the City flagged the funding gap from the start. Establishes the targets exist, not any outcome.
citations.quote: Current investments are not enough to achieve reduction targets and action is needed as the carbon deficit continues to grow under the current state.

items.title: 2023-2026 Carbon Budget Update Report (via CBC News)

citations.finding: The 2023-2026 Carbon Budget Update Report states 2023 emissions were 16.2 Mt versus a target of 13.4 Mt, and directly concludes that targets will not be achieved on the current trajectory.
citations.establishes: The City's official assessment that community emissions exceed targets and are off track.
citations.quote: If Edmonton's current emission trajectory continues, Edmonton's GHG reduction targets will not be achieved.

citations.finding: The Fall 2025 update states that actual emissions remained above forecast and target values. It reports a 2025 target of no more than 10.8 million tCO2e, requiring a 29 per cent reduction from 2024, and says the trend indicates that target will not be met.
citations.establishes: The missed 2024 trajectory was not an isolated comparison. The City's subsequent-year assessment also found no plausible path from current initiatives to the 2025 milestone.
citations.quote: There are no current initiatives or actions that will allow the necessary reductions to meet the target.
